Order 
Appellants have filed this appeal under Section 173 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1988 (hereinafter referred as "MV Act") being aggrieved by the award dated 27.08.2019 passed in Claim Case No.13/2019 challenging the quantum of assessment on the ground of improper assessment of income of deceased Kanchanbai.
02. The factum of liability of the Insurance Company due to death in the accident by insured vehicle is not under dispute.

03. Short facts of the case are that on 06.04.2017, the deceased Kanchanbai was going with her son Dinesh on motorcycle to Village Dudlai, when they reached near Bhaursa square at Indore-Bhopal highway, respondent No.2 came driving Tavera car bearing registration No.MP-09- NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24593 2 MA-7094-2019 BD-4434 in a rash and negligent manner and dashed into the motorcycle of Dinesh because of which both Dinesh and Kanchanbai fell from the motorcycle and got dragged to some distance.
Kanchanbai died while on the way to the hospital and Dinesh died at the spot itself.
An FIR was registered under Section 279, 337 and 304-A of IPC.
The appellants filed claim petitions before the Claims Tribunal under Section 166 of MV Act claiming compensation for the death of Kanchanbai.
The Claims Tribunal after considering the evidence available on record awarded a total sum of Rs.6,50,800/- to the appellants.

04. Learned counsel for the appellants has contended that the income as assessed by the Claims Tribunal is not proper in as much as she has been treated as a homemaker and her income has been taken on notional basis at Rs.6,000/- per month which is not even equivalent to the minimum Ranjit Singh vs Yogendra Singh on 2 September, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/22717746/
1 wages which was prescribed at the relevant time by the Labour Commissioner of State of M.P. as well as the State Legal Services Authority.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He further submits that the amount of consortium has not been awarded to other claimants except the widower.
Hence, he prays for enhancement of the compensation.

05. Per contra, learned counsel for the respondent/ Insurance Company submits that in fact no income of the deceased was pleaded or shown by the claimants thus the Claims Tribunal has assessed the income on notional basis at Rs.6,000/- per month which cannot be found fault with in absence of contrary material on record.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of appeal.
06. Heard learned counsel for the parties; perused the record.

07. From the finding of the award it is clear that the claimants did not NEUTRAL CITATION NO.
2025:MPHC-IND:24593 3 MA-7094-2019 claim any income of the deceased Kanchanbai.
The Claims Tribunal in Para 12 of the award has mentioned that nothing regarding income of the deceased has been brought on record.

On perusal of the documents and evidence available on record, it is clear that the Claims Tribunal has correctly recorded its finding however, while assessing the income of the deceased Kanchanbai, the Claims Tribunal was duty bound to consider all the aspects so as to arrive at the just compensation as mandated under Section 168 of the MV Act.

It is trite law that contribution of the homemaker cannot be considered less than the contribution of an earning member of the family thus, at any rate the notional income of the deceased could not have been taken lesser than the minimum wages prescribed for an unskilled labour at the relevant time.

The date of accident is 06.04.2017 and as per the guidelines of State Legal Services Authority at the relevant time, the minimum wages of an unskilled labour were Rs.7,125/- which is taken as the income of the deceased Kanchanbai.
08. As regards the question of consortium, the Claims Tribunal has correctly awarded the compensation for loss of consortium to the widower.

As per the law laid down by the Hon'ble Apex Court in the case of Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Nanu Ram, reported in 2019 ACJ SC 2782 only widow was entitled in the present case for such compensation.

entities.text: Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd. V/s Nanu Ram, reported in 2019 ACJ SC 2782
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: As regards the other heads from the award it is seen that just compensation has been awarded in other heads by the Claims Tribunal.

09. In view of the above analysis, based on modified income of the deceased the compensation for loss of dependency would now come to NEUTRAL CITATION NO. 2025:MPHC-IND:24593 4 MA-7094-2019 Rs.6,89,656/- and after deducting the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal, the present amount would come to Rs.1,08,856/- which is to be paid to the appellants over and above the amount already awarded by the Claims Tribunal.
This enhanced amount shall carry interest at the rate of 6 % per annum from the date of filing the application before the Claims Tribunal.
10. With the aforesaid, the present appeal stands disposed off.
